controlled_change: Three treatments: teammate56 socket/core+collated; original48 default mapping+default uncollated; io48 default mapping+collated. io48 versus original48 isolates file-handler choice on the same 48-rank source and mapping. The teammate56 arm is a complete peer-recipe comparison, not a single-factor contrast. Sources, physics, native runtime, fixed iteration settings, 56-CPU node, and 40-step horizon are held fixed within source.
question: On the same initialized 48-rank source and default MPI mapping, does collated I/O reduce native seconds per step versus default uncollated I/O, while comparing both 48-rank treatments with the teammate56 peer recipe?
rank_mapping: Original48 and io48 use default mapping; teammate56 alone uses --map-by socket --bind-to core. Per-rank file proofs and solver launcher reports are retained; no socket rank count is assumed.
